summary: The LLM landscape in 2026 is dominated by OpenAI's ChatGPT/GPT family with 53-55% of consumer web traffic, but enterprise API usage tells a different story with Anthropic's Claude leading at 40% of enterprise API calls. The market has fragmented significantly with strong competition from Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, DeepSeek, and a rising cohort of open-source challengers including Qwen, MiniMax, and Kimi models that now approach frontier performance at a fraction of the cost. Aggregator platforms like AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, and Google Vertex AI have become critical distribution channels, especially for enterprise adoption that often does not appear in direct-API usage statistics.

models.name: GPT-5 / ChatGPT (OpenAI family)
models.popularity_notes: Commands 53.9-55.5% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits as of mid-2026 (Similarweb) and is the anchor model on Azure OpenAI Service, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI, giving it unmatched aggregator reach across every major cloud.
strengths: Largest consumer mindshare and brand recognition globally
Ubiquitous availability across all major cloud aggregators (Azure OpenAI, AWS Bedrock, Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex)
Strong multi-step reasoning and conversational capability
Extensive plugin and tool-use ecosystem
Highest developer familiarity and documentation coverage
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise applications, conversational AI, coding assistance, and any deployment requiring broad cloud-platform availability

models.name: Claude (Anthropic family, incl. Claude 4 / Claude Fable 5.1)
models.popularity_notes: Leads enterprise API usage at 40% of enterprise API calls (Menlo Ventures 2025), holds 9.2-9.3% of worldwide chatbot web visits, and is available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, with Claude Fable 5.1 topping the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 66 as of September 2026.
strengths: Leads all vendors in enterprise API adoption at 40% share
Longest standard context window among closed models
Top-rated on safety, instruction-following, and document analysis
Available on AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex
Claude Fable 5.1 tops Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (score 66)
models.best_for: Enterprise document processing, long-context analysis, regulated-industry deployments, and safety-critical applications

models.name: Gemini (Google family, incl. Gemini 3.x Pro/Flash)
models.popularity_notes: Holds 25.6-27.9% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits as of mid-2026 (Similarweb), grew web traffic ~450% year-over-year, and benefits from native integration across Google Cloud Vertex AI, Workspace, and Android, as well as availability on AWS Bedrock.
strengths: Largest publicly available context window (up to 1M tokens)
Native integration with Google Cloud Vertex AI and Workspace ecosystem
Gemini 3.5 Flash achieves 78% on SWE-bench Verified
Strong multimodal capabilities across text, image, video, and audio
Rapid model iteration with competitive Flash-tier pricing
models.best_for: Multimodal enterprise applications, ultra-long document processing, Google Cloud-native deployments, and cost-efficient high-throughput tasks

models.name: Meta Llama 4 (Llama family)
models.popularity_notes: The most downloaded open-source model family on HuggingFace with billions of downloads cumulatively, available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, and Snowflake Cortex, making it the default open-weights choice for enterprises seeking self-hosted or managed deployment.
strengths: Most widely deployed open-source LLM family globally
Available on every major cloud aggregator (AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Vertex AI, IBM watsonx, Snowflake Cortex)
Full weights available for self-hosting and fine-tuning
Strong general reasoning per kairntech 2026 rankings
Zero licensing cost for most commercial use cases
models.best_for: Self-hosted enterprise deployments, fine-tuned domain-specific applications, cost-sensitive production workloads, and any use case requiring full model ownership

models.name: DeepSeek V4 / DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: Captured 24.4% of OpenRouter text requests in the week of September 21 2026 and holds 4.1% of worldwide chatbot web visits (May 2026), with DeepSeek-V4-Pro leading the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard on SWE-bench and LiveCodeBench benchmarks.
strengths: Leads Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard on SWE-bench bug-fixing and LiveCodeBench
24.4% share of OpenRouter API requests — highest of any single model on the platform
Developed at a fraction of typical LLM training costs
Open weights available for self-hosting
Highly competitive price-to-performance ratio for coding tasks
models.best_for: Developer-facing coding tools, code generation and debugging pipelines, cost-sensitive API deployments, and open-source enterprise integrations

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen family (Alibaba)
models.popularity_notes: Adopted by over 90,000 enterprises across consumer electronics, gaming, and other sectors (Shakudo 2026), with Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking and Qwen3.6-27B ranking among the top open-weights models for coding on the Onyx leaderboard, and available via Alibaba Cloud and OpenRouter.
strengths: 90,000+ enterprise adoptions globally
Top open-weights performance in multilingual tasks
Strong coding benchmarks with Qwen3.6-27B on Onyx leaderboard
MoE architecture enables high capability at lower serving cost
Wide availability through Alibaba Cloud, HuggingFace, and OpenRouter
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise applications, Asian-market deployments, cost-efficient coding and reasoning, and consumer electronics AI integration

models.name: Grok (xAI family, incl. Grok 3)
models.popularity_notes: Holds 2.4% of worldwide AI chatbot web visits as of May 2026 (Momentic), benefits from native integration with the X platform giving it a unique real-time data advantage, and Grok 3 is available via API with competitive pricing at $3.00/$15.00 per million tokens.
strengths: Native real-time integration with X (Twitter) platform and live web data
Rapidly growing user base through X Premium distribution
Competitive reasoning capabilities in the Grok 3 generation
Unique access to real-time social media context
Available via public API for developer integrations
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval, social media analysis, current-events-aware applications, and X platform integrations

models.name: Mistral (Mistral AI family, incl. Mistral Small 4 / Mistral Large)
models.popularity_notes: Mistral Small 4 (119B MoE, 6.5B active parameters, Apache 2.0) launched March 2026 and is consistently ranked among the most powerful open LLMs; available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex, making it the leading European open-source option with strong aggregator coverage.
strengths: Best-in-class price-performance among European open-source models
Available on AWS Bedrock, Azure AI, Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex
Apache 2.0 license for unrestricted commercial use
MoE architecture: 119B total but only 6.5B active params for efficiency
Combines instruct, reasoning, and coding in a single model
models.best_for: EU data-sovereignty deployments, cost-sensitive enterprise API workloads, coding and reasoning at low latency, and GDPR-compliant AI applications

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.popularity_notes: Ranks in the top tier of the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard (July 2026) for both bug-fixing and reasoning, launched between April and July 2026 alongside other frontier open models, and has gained rapid developer adoption on OpenRouter as a high-capability low-cost alternative.
strengths: Top-tier on Onyx leaderboard for real bug-fixing (SWE-bench) and reasoning
Massive 1M token context window at very low cost
Rapid adoption trajectory on OpenRouter aggregator
Competitive with frontier closed models on key benchmarks
Strong open-source community momentum since mid-2026 launch
models.best_for: Long-context document analysis, code review pipelines, cost-efficient reasoning workloads, and developers seeking open frontier-quality models

models.name: Kimi K2 / K2.6 (Moonshot AI)
models.popularity_notes: Kimi K2.6 ranks in the top 5 of the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard across bug-fixing, code generation, and reasoning categories as of July 2026, with Kimi K3 generating significant anticipation and available on OpenRouter for API access.
strengths: Top-5 on Onyx leaderboard for code generation, reasoning, and bug-fixing simultaneously
Strong agentic tool-use capabilities
Competitive open-weights model from a fast-moving Chinese AI lab
Available on OpenRouter for easy developer integration
Kimi K3 follow-up model already generating frontier-level benchmark interest
models.best_for: Agentic coding workflows, multi-step reasoning tasks, developers seeking open-weights frontier alternatives, and cost-optimized production deployments

models.name: GLM-5.2 (ChatGLM family)
models.popularity_notes: Achieves the highest GPQA Diamond score among open-source models on the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard (updated July 20 2026), with a 1M token context window and competitive pricing at $0.95/$3.00 per million tokens via API, placing it close to the top-10 cluster in developer adoption.
strengths: Highest GPQA Diamond score among open-source models (Onyx leaderboard, July 2026)
1M token context window at sub-$1 input pricing
Strong scientific and graduate-level reasoning capability
Fast inference at 347 tokens/second (Vellum leaderboard)
Open weights with competitive API pricing
models.best_for: Scientific research assistance, graduate-level reasoning, long-document summarization, and cost-efficient high-reasoning API workloads
